scope.reviewed: Reconciled allocation_plan against weight uploads, tied output reuse, optional bias buffers, workspace, fused scratch, KV storage, phase tables and activation-Q8 scratch. Checked multiplication/addition overflow handling, positive dimensions and kernel byte-extent limits.
Traced Qwen3 query_width independently from model width through QKV matrix views, fused slice offsets, Q/K normalization, RoPE, attention output, projection input and maximum activation scratch.

Checked fused bias precedence, complete separate-bias group activation and inactive partial-group behavior against the existing CPU/source contract; separate projections retain independent optional biases.
Checked per-head normalization indexing, shared per-head weights, GQA mapping, NeoX half-head pairing, phase indexing and the corrected F64 mean division.

Compared no-FMA SSE2 coefficients, reduction order, split-scale branches and four-lane softmax accumulation against frozen vec.h. Checked scalar F64 range reduction, explicit rounding conversions, SiLU scalar tails, F64 reciprocal-to-F32 order and masked/nonfinite score handling.
Inspected new conversion type validation, PTX spelling and interpreter behavior for F64-to-nearest-I32, I32-to-F64/U64 and U64-bit-to-F64 operations used by scalar exponential evaluation.

Checked position commit after successful finite outputs, cancellation boundaries, unused KV-row overwrite behavior, reset/truncate replay tests, provenance handling and the two exact RMS rounding regressions.

findings.problem: Computing the mean as F64 sum multiplied by a rounded F64 reciprocal can differ from frozen-source F64 division before the F32 cast for admitted non-power-of-two widths.
findings.source_contract: F32 element squares accumulated in F64; divide the sum by the row dimension in F64; cast to F32; add F32 epsilon; F32 square root and reciprocal; F32 normalization multiplications.
findings.verification: Counterexample independently evaluated using IEEE F32 roundings and F64 arithmetic in JavaScript and Python, and checked against the frozen source expression. The counterexample did not come from a Rust runtime output.
findings.correction: Both kernels now emit Binary::Div with the exact dimension converted to F64, replacing reciprocal multiplication.
findings.regression_expectation: The scalar test asserts exact scale bits 0x3f5105bc; the head test asserts every F32 output bit using that independently established scale.
findings.runtime_validation: The reviewer verified the corrected implementation and exact regression definitions. Final post-correction live CUDA execution results are owned and recorded separately by the integration task.

conclusion.disposition: One concrete numerical defect found and verified corrected in the reviewed snapshot; no additional blocking defects identified in the requested scope.
conclusion.evidence_type: Source inspection, independently evaluated arithmetic counterexample and regression-definition inspection.

limits: This is a source review of the identified snapshot, not a certification of the final integrated commit or completion of any global release gate.
The reviewer did not execute the final post-correction GPU matrix. Parent-reported earlier native/pretrained results were context, not substituted for that final execution.
Inspection did not prove universal bit identity between the scalar exponential polynomial and every host expf implementation or every finite F32 input.
Numerical reasoning is scoped to the frozen scalar MSVC and no-FMA SSE2 GNU profiles used by this work; other architectures and compiler math profiles were not certified.
Reviewed CUDA model admission is dense Llama/Qwen2/Qwen3 with its explicit dtype and graph limits. Other architectures, backend families and unsupported variants are outside this review.
No implementation or test source was edited by the reviewer while recording this evidence.
